summary.intent: Resolve open PR review comments on the batch upload pipeline PR, then merge it; afterward update planning docs (DEFERRED.md, FEATURES.md, README.md) and create a new filesystem specification document on a docs branch.
summary.outcome: All 4 review threads were triaged, fixed where valid, replied to, and resolved; the PR was merged to main. A docs branch (PR #419) was created with updated DEFERRED.md, FEATURES.md, README.md, and a new docs/FILESYSTEM_SPECIFICATION.md, with several follow-up corrections applied (stale/invalid deferred items removed, FUSE test rationale documented, vault v1 fields confirmed gone).

repo: Grafana Faro is the live error tracking solution (apps/web/src/lib/faro.ts) — not Sentry. Any deferred item referencing Sentry is stale.
Session replay is considered an anti-feature for this zero-knowledge privacy-focused product and is explicitly out of scope.
FUSE layer (crates/fuse/) has no unit tests by design — the OS integration plumbing is covered by the Desktop E2E suite instead, making unit mocking unreliable and unnecessary.
Vault v1 legacy fields were purged when staging was reset and a full-schema baseline migration was established; no DROP COLUMN migrations exist because the columns never appeared in the new schema.
Web Worker encryption (Phase 37) was fully implemented but the corresponding todo file was still sitting in .planning/todos/pending/ — it needed a manual move to done/.
Phases are tracked under .planning/phases/ with per-phase CONTEXT, PLAN, SUMMARY, RESEARCH, VALIDATION, and VERIFICATION docs.

CodeRabbit and GitHub Copilot both independently flagged the same lazy-file-reading architectural issue in useDropUpload.ts, which was already tracked as a deferred item from an earlier CodeRabbit review round.
The 3 failing integration tests in packages/sdk/src/__tests__/integration.test.ts require a live backend and are pre-existing — they are expected to fail in local CI.

code.finding: postMessage() and getWorker() can throw, leaving pending entries in the queue without cleanup. Fixed with try/catch that removes the pending entry on error.

Batch reads all files into memory before the SDK call. This is an architectural limitation — SDK accepts Uint8Array, not File/stream. Deferred: requires SDK contract change to accept File objects or a read callback.
JSDoc comment on uploadFiles() overstated memory bounding. Fixed to accurately describe the actual concurrency-bounded memory behavior.

workflow: When resolving PR review threads, use gh api graphql for fetching threads (isResolved filter) and resolving them, but use REST (gh api repos/.../pulls/.../comments) for posting replies — the --field flag (not -f) is required for integer fields like in_reply_to.

Deferred items lists accumulate stale entries quickly; each cleanup pass should verify against the actual codebase (grep for symbols, check file existence) rather than trusting the list at face value.

After a large merge (4802 insertions), planning docs (FEATURES.md, DEFERRED.md, README.md) typically need a dedicated cleanup pass — best done on a separate docs branch rather than mixed into feature PRs.

friction: The web worker encryption todo file was not moved to done/ when Phase 37 was completed — required a manual catch after the fact.

DEFERRED.md had accumulated multiple invalid entries: already-implemented items (Grafana Faro), explicitly out-of-scope items (session replay), and premature infrastructure items (production Kubo hardening) — required a separate review pass with user correction.
git push initially failed on the docs branch and required a retry.
Edit tool reformatted markdown table column widths, making subsequent edits harder to target without re-reading the raw file with bash cat -n.
open_items: Lazy file reading in useDropUpload.ts (useDropUpload.ts:140) — SDK needs to accept File objects or a read callback instead of Uint8Array to avoid reading all files into memory before the upload call.
Batch upload is not yet implemented in the Rust SDK — noted in updated FEATURES.md feature matrix.

Cross-platform filesystem edge cases documented in docs/FILESYSTEM_SPECIFICATION.md: case-insensitive collision handling on Windows/macOS HFS+, Windows reserved names (CON, PRN, etc.), trailing dot stripping on Windows, emoji normalization across platforms, and symlink/alias behavior differences.
Desktop E2E test suite coverage for FUSE write operations — covered by existing Desktop E2E but not explicitly enumerated in the feature matrix.
Observability deferred items remain: structured log shipping pipeline, distributed tracing across API/IPFS/SDK boundaries, and performance budget alerting.
Upload pipeline deferred items: resumable uploads (tus protocol), per-file granular progress events in SDK, upload queue persistence across page reloads.
